**DK26.6** is a specific medical diagnosis code used within the Danish healthcare system to classify a chronic or unspecified duodenal ulcer complicated by both hemorrhage and perforation [^src1]. In the context of the national clinical quality databases managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this code serves as a critical data point for monitoring severe adverse events in patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1] [^src2].

Because patients treated for atrial fibrillation are frequently prescribed anticoagulant therapies, they face an elevated risk of major bleeding complications. To accurately measure the incidence of severe bleeding as a clinical quality indicator, the national registry tracks a comprehensive list of diagnostic codes across multiple bodily systems [^src1]. DK26.6 is one of the specific codes used to identify gastrointestinal bleeding events, grouped alongside other gastric and intestinal codes like [[dk25-0|DK25.0]], [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]], [[dk92-0|DK92.0]], and [[dk92-2|DK92.2]] [^src1]. The broader bleeding indicator also captures intracranial hemorrhages (using codes such as [[di60|DI60]] through [[ds066|DS066]]) as well as respiratory and urinary tract bleeding (using codes like [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. 

The precise definition and inclusion of DK26.6 in these quality indicators are formally outlined in the annual methodology and reporting documents for the Atrial Fibrillation database (Atrieflimren i Danmark), ensuring standardized and comparable health data collection across all Danish regions [^src1] [^src2].
